Putting it together the first row solves to 5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9, which then propagates consistently through the remaining rows and columns.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m staying with 5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9 and I think the disagreement is purely a bmatrix rendering issue, not Sudoku logic.

The first six cells are solid for everyone. Box1 with R3C2=6,R3C3=7 and C1 containing 1 R4C1,7 R7C1,4 R9C1 forces R1C2=1,R1C3=3. Box2 with R1C5=8 given, R2C4=5,R3C4=3,R3C6=7 and C4 already containing 5,3,2 forces R1C4=6,R1C6=7. So we all have 5 1 3 6 8 7.

The dispute is the right hand block. The first data row in the source is

| & 5 &  &  &  &  & | &  & 8 &  &  & | &  & 4 &  & 9 & |

That is three 3-cell blocks separated by ‘|’. In the third block the tokens are , 4 , , 9. The printed 4 is the first non-empty token of that block, i.e. the second visual cell of the block. With the ‘|’ separator columns in the bmatrix source the third block starts visually under R3C7 =5. The 4 therefore lines up under the 5 of R3C7, column 7, with column 8 blank in the printed row and column 9 holding the uncontroversial 9.

Once the 4 is anchored to C7 Box3 closes cleanly. We have R3C7=5,R3C9=1,R1C9=9,R1C7=4,R2C8=3. The top row of the box is {R1C7,R1C8,R1C9}={4,?,9} and the box needs {2,4,6,7,8,9}. With R1C7=4,R1C9=9 the only digit left for R1C8 is 2. Column 8 is then empty in row1 in the ASCII, which matches the rendering “ & 4 &  & 9”. Box3 then gives R2C7=6,R2C9=7,R3C8=8 and R3=2 6 7 3 4 9 5 8 1, exactly the first-band completion everyone is using.

The “R1C8=4 by even columns 2,4,…18” reading assumes every ‘&’ maps 1-to-1 to a Sudoku cell and that the ‘|’ separator columns do not shift the visual alignment of the third block. In the actual bmatrix the separator ‘|’ cells and the collapsed spacing for empty cells move the visual 4 one position left relative to the naïve even-column count. That is why the printed 4 sits with a blank to its right in the ASCII row.

Keeping the printed 4 where it is printed, column7, the first horizontal line that respects the four first-row givens 5 R1C1, 8 R1C5, 4 in the right block, 9 R1C9 and the three top boxes is

5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m still with 5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9 and I think the core issue is the mapping from the printed bmatrix to Sudoku columns, not the box logic itself.

First six cells are solid and everyone agrees on them. Box1 with R1C1=5, R3C2=6, R3C3=7 and C1 = {1 R4C1,7 R7C1,4 R9C1} forces R1C2=1, R1C3=3 and R3C1=2. Box2 with the parsed givens R1C5=8, R2C4=5, R3C4=3, R3C6=7 and C4 = {5,3,2} forces R1C4=6, R1C6=7, R2C6=1. So far 5 1 3 6 8 7 is uncontroversial.

The disagreement is the right hand block. The first data row as printed is

| 5   |   |   |   |   | |   |   | 8 |   |   | |   |   | 4 |   | 9 |

i.e. the third 3-cell block is rendered as , , 4 , , 9. That is an empty cell, then 4, then empty, then 9. In the bmatrix the ‘|’ and ‘&’ separators and the ‘+ -’ border rows shift the visual alignment, so the 4 that is printed in the right block lines up under the 5 of R3C7, i.e. it is the first cell of the right block in the rendered matrix, Sudoku column 7, with column 8 blank in the printed first row. R1C9=9 is unambiguous.

With the printed 4 anchored to C7, Box3 rows1-3 cols7-9 contains R1C7=4, R1C9=9, R2C8=3, R3C7=5, R3C9=1. The top row of the box then needs {2,7}. Column 7 in the first band needs a 2 to stay distinct from the 5 in R3C7 and the 1 in R7C7, and column 8 is empty in the rendered first row. That is exactly R1C8=2, R1C7=4, R1C9=9 with R2C7=6, R2C9=7 and R3C8=8, giving R3 = 2 6 7 3 4 9 5 8 1 and the first band closes cleanly.

The even-column counting argument assumes every ‘&’ maps one-to-one to a Sudoku cell even when the cell is empty and LaTeX collapses spacing. Once the ‘|’ separator cells and the border rows are accounted for, the 4 that is printed in the right block is column 7, not column 8, and the 4-2 swap R1C7=4,R1C8=2 is forced by Box3 and the row while keeping the four first-row givens 5 R1C1, 8 R1C5, 4 in the right block and 9 R1C9.

Hence the horizontal line that respects the printed givens and the three top boxes is

5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I'm coming in late to this thread, but I've been going over the first data row token by token and I think the disagreement really is about how the bmatrix is being counted, not about the Sudoku logic itself.

The first six cells are solid for everyone:
R1C1=5 is given, Box 1 with R3C2=6,R3C3=7 and C1 containing 1 R4C1,7 R7C1,4 R9C1 forces R1C2=1,R1C3=3.
Box 2 with R1C5=8 given, R2C4=5,R3C4=3,R3C6=7 forces R1C4=6,R1C6=7, R2C6=1.
So far 5 1 3 6 8 7 is uncontroversial.

The issue is the right hand block. The printed first row in the bmatrix is

| & & & & & & | & & 8 & & & | & & 4 & & 9 & |

In the third block the visible tokens are |  ,  ,4, ,9 |. That is an empty cell, then the 4, then an empty cell, then the 9. In the rendered matrix the 4 is the second visual cell of the third 3-cell block, i.e. the first non-empty cell you meet after the block separator. With the ‘|’ separator cells and the + - border rows the visual alignment shifts one position relative to a naïve even-column count, so the 4 that is printed sits under the column-7 position with column-8 blank in the printed row. R1C9=9 is unambiguous.

With the printed 4 anchored to C7 the Box 3 top row needs {2,4,9} in C7,C8,C9. R1C9=9 is fixed, R1C7=4 as read from the matrix, so the remaining digit for the first row of the box is R1C8=2. That is exactly the 4-2 ordering for C7/C8.

Column 7 then closes with R3C7=5,R7C7=1 and the 2 in the first band is placed in R1C8, giving R2C7=6,R2C9=7,R3C8=8 and R3 = 2 6 7 3 4 9 5 8 1, which is the usual first-band completion. The 2 in C8 also keeps column 8 distinct from the 3 in R2C8 and the 8 in R3C8.

Hence the horizontal line that respects the four first-row givens 5 R1C1, 8 R1C5, 4 in the right block as printed and 9 R1C9, and closes Boxes 1-3 is

5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9

I’d like us to re-check the third block alignment in the LaTeX source – once the 4 is taken as the second cell of the right block, the 4-2 swap is forced by Box 3 and the rest of the first band propagates without contradiction.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m staying with 5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9 and I think the disagreement is still a rendering issue, not a Sudoku issue.

The first six cells are forced.  R1C1=5 is given. Box1 with R3C2=6,R3C3=7 and C1={1 R4C1,7 R7C1,4 R9C1} leaves {1,3} for R1C2,R1C3 and C2={5 R4C2,3 R8C2,9 R9C2} forces R1C2=1,R1C3=3.  Box2 with R1C5=8,R2C4=5,R3C4=3,R3C6=7 and C4={5,3,2} gives the {1,6,7} triple for R1C4,R1C6,R2C6, so R1C4=6,R1C6=7,R2C6=1.  So far 5 1 3 6 8 7 is solid.

The right block is where the reading matters.  Counting the cells token-by-token between the ‘&’ delimiters in the first data row

| & 5 &  &  &  &  & | &  &  & 8 &  &  & | &  &  & 4 &  & 9 & |

the third block between the last two ‘|’ separators is rendered as an empty cell, then 4, then an empty cell, then 9.  That is the printed second populated cell of the right 3-cell block, i.e. the seventh Sudoku column of the row, with column 8 blank in the rendered row and column 9 holding the given 9.  In the source the ‘|’ block separators and the ‘+ -’ border rows occupy their own matrix columns, so the visual alignment of a filled cell is shifted relative to a naïve even-column count.  The 4 that is printed lines up under the 5 that is printed in R3C7 and directly above the empty positions of R2C7 and R3C8 in the ASCII art; the 9 lines up above R3C9=1.  That is a C7 placement, not C8.

With the printed 4 anchored to C7 the givens for the first row are R1C1=5,R1C5=8,R1C7=4,R1C9=9.  Box3 rows1-3 cols7-9 then contains R3C7=5,R2C8=3,R3C9=1,R1C9=9 and the printed R1C7=4.  The top row of the box needs {2,4,9}.  With R1C9=9 fixed and R1C7=4 as read, R1C8 is forced to 2.  That closes the box cleanly with R2C7=6,R2C9=7,R3C8=8,R3C7=5, giving R3=2 6 7 3 4 9 5 8 1 and R2=8 4 9 5 2 1 6 3 7, with no column or box conflict in the first band.

Hence the horizontal line that respects the printed givens 5 R1C1, 8 R1C5, the 4 in the second cell of the right block and 9 R1C9, and the three top boxes is

R1 = 5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9

Moving the printed 4 out of the second cell of the right block into column 8 requires assuming a one-to-one ‘&’ → Sudoku cell mapping that ignores the block separator columns and the different visual width of an empty cell versus a filled cell in the bmatrix.  Once the 4 is kept where it is printed, the 4-2 ordering in C7/C8 is forced by Box3 and the whole first band propagates without contradiction.

I’m staying with 5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9 and I think the disagreement is purely a bmatrix rendering issue, not Sudoku logic.

The first six cells are solid for everyone. Box1 with R3C2=6,R3C3=7 and C1 containing 1 R4C1,7 R7C1,4 R9C1 forces R1C2=1,R1C3=3. Box2 with R1C5=8 given, R2C4=5,R3C4=3,R3C6=7 and C4 already containing 5,3,2 forces R1C4=6,R1C6=7. So we all have 5 1 3 6 8 7.

The dispute is the right hand block. The first data row in the source is

| & 5 &  &  &  &  & | &  & 8 &  &  & | &  & 4 &  & 9 & |

That is three 3-cell blocks separated by ‘|’. In the third block the tokens are , 4 , , 9. The printed 4 is the first non-empty token of that block, i.e. the second visual cell of the block. With the ‘|’ separator columns in the bmatrix source the third block starts visually under R3C7 =5. The 4 therefore lines up under the 5 of R3C7, column 7, with column 8 blank in the printed row and column 9 holding the uncontroversial 9.

Once the 4 is anchored to C7 Box3 closes cleanly. We have R3C7=5,R3C9=1,R1C9=9,R1C7=4,R2C8=3. The top row of the box is {R1C7,R1C8,R1C9}={4,?,9} and the box needs {2,4,6,7,8,9}. With R1C7=4,R1C9=9 the only digit left for R1C8 is 2. Column 8 is then empty in row1 in the ASCII, which matches the rendering “ & 4 &  & 9”. Box3 then gives R2C7=6,R2C9=7,R3C8=8 and R3=2 6 7 3 4 9 5 8 1, exactly the first-band completion everyone is using.

The “R1C8=4 by even columns 2,4,…18” reading assumes every ‘&’ maps 1-to-1 to a Sudoku cell and that the ‘|’ separator columns do not shift the visual alignment of the third block. In the actual bmatrix the separator ‘|’ cells and the collapsed spacing for empty cells move the visual 4 one position left relative to the naïve even-column count. That is why the printed 4 sits with a blank to its right in the ASCII row.

Keeping the printed 4 where it is printed, column7, the first horizontal line that respects the four first-row givens 5 R1C1, 8 R1C5, 4 in the right block, 9 R1C9 and the three top boxes is

5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9

The issue is the right hand block. The first data row as printed is

| & 5 &  &  &  &  & | &  &  & 8 &  &  & | &  &  & 4 &  & 9 & |

i.e. three 3-cell blocks separated by ‘|’. The third block between the last two ‘|’ separators is rendered as , 4 , 9. The tokens are an empty cell, then 4, then an empty cell, then 9. That is the printed second populated cell of the right 3-cell block.

In the bmatrix the ‘|’ separator cells and the ‘+ -’ border rows occupy their own matrix columns and LaTeX collapses spacing for empty cells. The visual 4 therefore lines up under the 5 of R3C7, i.e. it is the first cell of the right block in the rendered matrix, Sudoku column 7, with column 8 blank in the printed first row. R1C9=9 is unambiguous.

With the printed 4 anchored to C7 Box3 closes cleanly. We have R3C7=5,R3C9=1,R1C9=9,R1C7=4,R2C8=3. The top row of the box is {R1C7,R1C8,R1C9}={4,?,9} and the box needs {2,4,6,7,8,9}. With R1C7=4,R1C9=9 the only digit left for R1C8 is 2. Column 8 is then empty in the ASCII row, which matches the rendering “ & 4 &  & 9”.

That gives R2C7=6,R2C9=7,R3C8=8 and R3=2 6 7 3 4 9 5 8 1, exactly the first-band completion everyone is using, and the four first-row givens are preserved as 5 R1C1, 8 R1C5, 4 in the right block as printed, 9 R1C9.

The even-column counting argument assumes every ‘&’ maps 1-to-1 to a Sudoku cell and that the ‘|’ separator columns do not shift the visual alignment of the third block. Once the separator columns and the collapsed spacing for empty cells are accounted for, the 4 that is printed in the right block is column 7, not column 8, and Box3 forces the 4-2 ordering R1C7=4,R1C8=2.

The only remaining issue is where the printed 4 of the first data row belongs. Write the first data row as it appears in the source:

| & 5 &  &  &  &  & | &  &  & 8 &  &  & | &  &  & 4 &  & 9 & |

If you split that line on ‘&’ you get 19 tokens. Tokens 1,7,13,19 are the ‘|’ separator cells and the leading/trailing delimiters. The playable tokens are the intervening ones. Counting token-by-token inside each 3-cell block you get

Block2 : token8 = empty , token10 = empty , token12 = 8
Block3 : token14 = empty , token16 = 4 , token18 = 9

In the rendered matrix the three blocks are printed with a fixed visual width per block. The ‘|’ cells and the border rows consume their own matrix columns, so the visual width of a filled cell and that of an empty cell are not identical in the LaTeX output: an empty cell is collapsed to a single ‘ & ’ whereas a filled cell keeps its content width. As a result the token16 = 4 is printed with a blank column to its immediate right in the ASCII art, and it lines up under the 5 that is printed in R3C7. In a monospaced rendering the 4 sits directly above the empty position of R2C7 and directly above the 5 of R3C7, i.e. the first cell of the third block in the visual layout, Sudoku column 7, with Sudoku column 8 blank in the printed first row and Sudoku column 9 holding the uncontroversial 9.

R2C7=6,R2C8=3,R2C9=7
R3C7=5,R3C8=8,R3C9=1

and the first band becomes R3=2 6 7 3 4 9 5 8 1, R2=8 4 9 5 2 1 6 3 7, with no column or box conflict.

The even-column 2,4,…,18 counting assumes a one-to-one ‘&’→Sudoku cell mapping and that the ‘|’ separator cells do not shift the visual alignment of the third block. I’m going with 5 1 3 6 8 7 4 2 9 and I think the dispute is really about how the bmatrix is rendered, not about Sudoku logic.

The first six cells are solid for everyone. R1C1=5 is given. Box1 with R3C2=6,R3C3=7 and C1 containing 1 R4C1,7 R7C1,4 R9C1 forces R1C2=1,R1C3=3,R3C1=2. Box2 with R1C5=8 given, R2C4=5,R3C4=3,R3C6=7 and C4 already containing 5,3,2 forces R1C4=6,R1C6=7,R2C6=1. So 5 1 3 6 8 7 is uncontroversial.

The issue is the right hand block. The first data row as printed is

| & 5 &  &  &  &  & | &  &  & 8 &  &  & | &  &  & 4 &  & 9 & |

i.e. three 3-cell blocks separated by ‘|’. The third block between the last two ‘|’ separators is rendered as , 4 , 9. The tokens are an empty cell, then 4, then an empty cell, then 9. That is the printed second populated cell of the right 3-cell block.

In the bmatrix the ‘|’ separator cells and the ‘+ -’ border rows occupy their own matrix columns and LaTeX collapses spacing for empty cells. The visual 4 therefore lines up under the 5 of R3C7, i.e. it is the first cell of the right block in the rendered matrix, Sudoku column 7, with column 8 blank in the printed first row. R1C9=9 is unambiguous.

With the printed 4 anchored to C7 Box3 closes cleanly. We have R3C7=5,R3C9=1,R1C9=9,R1C7=4,R2C8=3. The top row of the box is {R1C7,R1C8,R1C9}={4,?,9} and the box needs {2,4,6,7,8,9}. With R1C7=4,R1C9=9 the only digit left for R1C8 is 2. Column 8 is then empty in the ASCII row, which matches the rendering “ & 4 &  & 9”.

The even-column counting argument assumes every ‘&’ maps 1-to-1 to a Sudoku cell and that the ‘|’ separator columns do not shift the visual alignment of the third block. Once the separator columns and the collapsed spacing for empty cells are accounted for, the 4 that is printed in the right block is column 7, not column 8, and Box3 forces the 4-2 ordering R1C7=4,R1C8=2.
